Here the next outgoing value is −1. Removing it raises the sum from 4 to 5 and exposes the length-1 valid range [5]. For the general shortest-at-least problem with signed values, a standard alternative combines prefix sums with a monotonic deque: the deque stores candidate start boundaries in increasing prefix-sum order, removes older tail candidates when the current later prefix is no larger and therefore dominates them, and removes front candidates when the current-prefix difference reaches T. That mechanism does not assume one left pointer remains safe.
